prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2] SLA tiers (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Tier" · longest unbreakable word 84px · one-line width 105px
  col 2: header "Monthly uptime commitment" · longest unbreakable word 91px · one-line width 207px
  col 3: header "Service credit" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 100px
  col 4: header "Support channels" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 531px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare SLA tiers by uptime commitment, service credit, and available support.","reading":"Readers scan tier names down the first column, compare commitments and credits across rows, then read support details within each tier. Longer support descriptions will set row heights, giving headers and other cells room to wrap where needed.","groups":["Monthly uptime commitment and service credit are comparable numeric terms; their values should be easy to scan down their columns.","Tier identifies each row, while support channels describe the service available for that tier."],"keep_intact":["Tier names, including Mission-critical","Uptime percentages and service credit percentages","Individual words and identifiers"],"may_wrap":["Monthly uptime commitment and Service credit headers at word boundaries","Support channel descriptions at word boundaries"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [126, 170, 112, 311] · table 720×216px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [110, 228, 100, 281] · table 720×239px · row heights [60, 36, 83, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [125, 145, 95, 354] · table 720×216px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 2/4 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
